# LEDGER — the durable record under PROTOCOL v4

Coordinator-only. Append-only. ONE LINE per ruling, landing or stamp, oldest first, in the form
`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM · KIND · SHA · one sentence` where KIND is RULING, LANDING or STAMP.
A lane's tick reads the tail since its last tick — a few lines — and nothing else of the channel;
`.claude/coord-scripts/fleet-read.sh <LANE> [SINCE]` prints exactly those lines after the inbox.
Never rewrite a line: a correction is a NEW line that names the line it corrects.

Layout comes from GoFieldOffsets of the darwin-emitted types, as on linux. POINTER-BEARING STRUCTS, RULED (b): a NIL pointer field encodes as 0, which is exactly what Go passes; a non-nil pointer field leaves that argument's token in place, so libc answers EFAULT, as (a) does. The linux-style panic (c) is REJECTED for darwin, because it would turn a kqueue or sendmsg errno into a crash. 2026-09-27 12:03 · RULING · a7dc4570d3 · THE PANIC-PATH FRAME DESIGN (R's DESIGN-panic-stack-frames.md, claude/r-panic-frames-design a7dc4570d3; P2 reviewed the frame half, inbox e3a5725cff) is APPROVED as option B with P2's FOUR CHANGES, to be cut AFTER M3 (it lands on M3's reshaped walk). THE DESIGN: splice Go's LOGICAL panicking stack into captureCallers, with no emission change: a per-thread stack of deferred sequences, a per-panic own-site trace, and a per-panic kind (a fault gives panicmem and sigpanic, a divide gives panicdivide); GoFrame.Run is NoInlining. Option A (running defers inside the exception filter) is rejected on R's evidence: a panic thrown inside a filter is swallowed by the CLR, cleanup order inverts against non-Go finally blocks, and it needs an emission change in every deferring function. Disclosure is kept only for deferreturn (the WithLoop form). GO'S OWN ANSWER, measured by P2 (linux amd64, go1.24.13, Callers from the deferred call after recover): plain panic gives func1, runtime.gopanic panic.go:792, the test, tRunner, goexit; a nil dereference adds runtime.panicmem panic.go:262 and runtime.sigpanic signal_unix.go:925 above the test at its faulting line; a divide adds runtime.panicdivide panic.go:241; a nil deferred func in a loop adds runtime.deferreturn panic.go:610. THE CHANGES, all required in the cut: (1) PAIRING: push one entry for EVERY GoFrame.Run activation that runs deferred calls (its m_count > 0 branch), holding that frame's OWN panic or null, because a Run frame is on the stack for a normal return too. Positional pairing mis-splices one sequence too high when a panic's deferred call reaches a helper that defers and calls Callers. When a deferred call's panic REPLACES the handled one inside one Run (the aborted-panic shape), that entry is updated. The record's "nothing on the no-panic path" becomes "one push and pop per deferring return, beside the existing save and restore". (2) OWNER FRAME: SiteTrace is the raised exception's OWN trace, as caught by the owning frame, never the inherited PanicTrace. Its last Go frame is the owner and is dropped, with an ASSERTION that it equals the next live Go frame of the walk; on a mismatch nothing is spliced and today's stack is answered, because a missing splice is a known divergence and a wrong one is a silent lie. (3) Spliced frames go through M3's SAME skip and capacity path and are interned with internRootFrame (one PC per Go call site, GOROOT-relative file names); R's red arms are read on the M3 base. (4) Run frames are matched by MethodBase identity, never by name; a live walk of the converted runtime.gopanic interning a second record is named at the site. COVERAGE: TestCallersPanic, DoublePanic, NilPointerPanic, DivZeroPanic and DeferNilFuncPanic; the WithLoop residual stays a disclosure, and if the converter's hint is ever cut it states Go's open-coding rule in full. Not covered, stated: CPU-profile stacks sampled inside a deferred call (the sampler walks through EventPipe, not captureCallers). ORDER: R's seat (iii), then P2's M3, then B (R), with P2 reviewing the cut.
